subject: SOW errata, ops guardrails and change-order next steps
messages:
From: Mike Torres <mike.torres@bluehaven.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@bluehaven.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOW errata and requested guardrails for upcoming change order

Hi Avery / Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We pulled the SOW and found a few small but material items we need clarified before we sign the change order:

- Section 2.3 (Data retention) currently reads "retention per default platform settings" — we need this to explicitly state 90 days for logs, 365 days for customer embeddings, and an option for extended retention with a pricing add-on.
- Section 4.1 (Monitoring & incident escalation) doesn't list a concrete escalation SLA or contact-path for P1 incidents — Bluehaven needs a 30-minute on-call response for P1s and an outline of escalation steps.
- Exhibit C (Rollforward/rollback) appears to reference a different product SKU; we need the rollback path to be unconditional for config-driven rollbacks during the first 30 days post-deploy.

Attached: SOW_Errata_v1.pdf (annotated). We are OK with the proposed capacity bump, but procurement wants the above clarified in the SOW and captured as a short change order or amendment before legal signs.

Target timeline: we'd like this finalized and routed to DocuSign by next Friday (2026-06-18). Can your legal team propose redlines? Ops will want a brief runbook for the rollback.

Thanks,

Mike Torres
Head of Infrastructure, Bluehaven AI
mike.torres@bluehaven.ai
+1 (415) 555-0194

Subject: Re: SOW errata and requested guardrails for upcoming change order

Mike / team — attaching our proposed redline and a short change-order draft. Summary of proposed contract language below; full redline is in the attachment (SOW_redline_20260611.docx).

Key edits (summary):
- Data retention (Section 2.3): Inserted explicit buckets: "Operational logs: 90 days; Customer embeddings: 365 days. Extended retention available via Exhibit F (pricing addendum)." Added customer opt-in checkbox for extended retention and a reference to KMS handling for long-term keys.
- Incident escalation (Section 4.1 / Exhibit G): Added a P1 definition and SLA: "P1 — critical production outage: Redwood response within 30 minutes during support hours; on-call escalation to engineering manager within 60 minutes; weekly incident summary for first 30 days post-incident."
- Rollback & rollforward (Exhibit C): Replaced the incorrect SKU reference. Added rollback language: "Customer may request an automated configuration rollback within 30 calendar days post-deploy; Redwood will initiate rollback within 2 hours provided rollback triggers are met in the runbook. Rollback will not be used to revert customer-initiated irreversible data-migration operations."

Open items for Bluehaven to confirm:
1) Does the 30/365 retention split work, or would you prefer 180 days for embeddings as a compromise?
2) Is 2 hours an acceptable commitment for initiating rollback, or do you require a faster window?

We also added a short clause to the change order about retroactive credits if the deployed capacity does not meet throughput targets for the first 14 days (credit formula in §2 of the change order). Please review.

Next steps: If you confirm retention and rollback timing, we'll incorporate any pricing tweaks and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOW errata and requested guardrails for upcoming change order

Stephanie / Avery — this looks good and thanks for the quick turnaround. Two quick items from procurement:

1) Retention: Bluehaven will accept the 90 days / 365 days split as proposed. No change required.
2) Pricing: Procurement wants the retroactive-credit language to apply only if throughput is below 70% of the committed baseline (not 100%); can you tweak §2 of the change order to reflect the 70% threshold?

If you can make that one edit we'll confirm and route the packet through procurement. We're aiming to sign the DocuSign envelope by 2026-06-18; we've started our internal PO and budget approvals in parallel.

Also attaching a draft change-order PDF with a procurement cover page — if you prefer we can do an e-sign packet once the revision is made.

Best,

Mike Torres
